issue.title: Generated CLI reference pages depend on the generating Python's argparse (3.12 vs 3.13+), so docs/reference/cli flip-flops and docs-gen-check fails on the other interpreter
issue.description:
`tools/render_cli` renders the committed `docs/reference/cli/*.md` pages from argparse help, and argparse's usage formatting differs between Python 3.12 and 3.13+. The pages therefore flip-flop with the Python version of whoever runs `just docs-gen`, and `just docs-gen-check` (run by `just check` / `just check-full`, never by CI) fails on the other interpreter.

Evidence (sase-1lh lander, master 97825eee1d):
- Phases sase-1lh.1 (note #2), sase-1lh.4 (note #1), and sase-1lh.5 (note #1) each saw `docs-gen-check` fail "identically on clean base" with CLI usage diffs on their Python 3.14 venvs.
- Commit e69c455bd6 (sase-1lh.4) then regenerated 18 pages under docs/reference/cli/ on Python 3.14. Now `tools/render_cli --check` passes on the 3.14.7 `.venv`, fails on exactly those 18 files under Python 3.12.13 (the drift is line-for-line the reverse of that commit's CLI-doc diff), and fails on 5 files under 3.13.
- Differences: 3.13+ keeps a subparser `...` on the choices line and renders non-adjacent mutually exclusive groups as `[-a | -M | -p NAME]`, where 3.12 lists the options separately.
- CI (Python 3.12) never runs docs-gen-check, so the drift is invisible to Master Gate and Full CI; it only reds local `just check` for agents on the "wrong" interpreter, which several phase agents misread as docs-epic drift.

Fix direction: make the generated output independent of the interpreter (normalize usage text in render_cli, or pin the generator to one interpreter and make docs-gen-check use it), then regenerate once. Related: sase-14p (a test that hard-codes the 3.13 argparse spelling).

task_type_fields.impact: Local just check reds for any agent whose venv Python differs from the last regenerator; regenerated pages churn in unrelated commits (e69c455bd6).
task_type_fields.repro: Run tools/render_cli --check with a Python 3.12 interpreter and then with the Python 3.14 .venv on the same tree (master 97825eee1d): 3.12 reports 18 drifted pages, 3.13 reports 5, 3.14 reports none.

issue.creation_reason: Three sase-1lh phases (sase-1lh.1, sase-1lh.4, sase-1lh.5) proposed this as clean-base docs-gen-check drift; the sase-1lh lander traced it to argparse version differences in tools/render_cli output.

payload.description: Same root cause class: argparse help/usage spelling differs between Python 3.12 and 3.13+
